reason: Both identify flat net activations, signup-triggered reward, fraud, and fix by paying on activation plus product credit. Answer A has a reasoning flaw: it asserts "100% zero-intent signups" and referred activation ~0% under an assumption, then contradicts itself with a caveat. It also says "zero-intent" overconfidently. Answer B is more careful and adds decision-relevant items: the cohort-age measurement artifact, referrals-per-referrer concentration (touching on segmenting referrers), a KPI switch to cost per activated user and incremental activations, a payout delay, and a kill criterion. Those would change what the asker does next. B better covers the key points (measure activated users per cohort, referrer segmentation). A's product-credit and double-sided points are also in B. B wins.
